solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Refined Europeans earl initially dismissed (8)

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each of the next two words gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of dismissed, also governed by 'initially'

annotation.surface: A snobbish account of cultured continentals who snubbed a visiting earl.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initially' reaches back over both earl and dismissed, so each gives its first letter; reading 'dismissed' as a deletion instruction is the trap.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: polish is the finish on manners and taste, so a person with it is cultured and refined.

entries.clue: Two in eight old people accepted topless bars (7)

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so O and MEN take the bars inside them
topless means without a top, so the word loses its first letter

annotation.surface: Elderly folk sharing a table at a topless bar.
annotation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing boat with a crew of eight, so 'two in eight' means two of its crew. Bars loses its top before going inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: an eight is a racing boat rowed by eight people, so any two of its crew fit.

entries.clue: Diamonds? Spotty types have no need of them! (3)

indicators.note: people who have no need of something do without it, so DICE does without its D

blocks.note: 'them' points back to Diamonds, d in card notation; removed from DICE

annotation.surface: A jibe that people with acne have no use for jewellery.
annotation.walkthrough: Diamonds does double duty: it is the definition and, through 'them', the card-suit abbreviation D taken out of DICE.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense from the criminal underworld: diamonds, glittering and cold-looking, are called by this name.

entries.clue: Fresher dwelling (renovated) is clean and freehold (4,2,9)

indicators.note: a renovated building is rebuilt inside, so the letters are rebuilt into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: An estate agent's blurb for a refurbished house, clean and owned outright.
annotation.walkthrough: A fresher is a first-year university student in Britain, not a comparative of fresh, and the fodder is split around the anagram indicator and the link word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the student accommodation block where first-year university students usually live.

entries.clue: Fancy Best missing header with Germany in lead (5)

indicators.note: a header is the top of a page or column; missing it, the word loses its first letter
to be in the lead is to be at the front, so D goes first

blocks.note: D = Germany, the international vehicle code
CREAM (the best) without its first letter

annotation.surface: A football report: a star player without a headed goal while Germany lead.
annotation.walkthrough: The football words (header, lead, Germany) paint a match; 'header' is just the first letter of CREAM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to fancy doing something is to wish for or imagine it.

entries.clue: A rugby player touring Belgium and Britain (6)

indicators.note: a touring side travels round a country, so LION goes around B

blocks.note: a Lion plays for the British and Irish Lions

annotation.surface: A British Lions rugby player on tour in Belgium and Britain.
annotation.walkthrough: The British and Irish Lions are a touring rugby team, so 'touring' fits both surface and mechanism.
annotation.definitionFit: A poetic and archaic name for Britain, still used by some football clubs.

entries.clue: Breeder and trainer mad about one ultimately? (8,7)

definitions.text: Breeder and trainer mad about one ultimately?

indicators.note: mad means crazed and disordered, so the letters lose their sensible order
about means surrounding, so the jumble sits around the E
ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of one is used

blocks.note: last letter of one, surrounded by the jumble

annotation.surface: A dog breeder and trainer who dote on one particular animal.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the dog a devoted breeder and trainer might be mad about. 'And' joins the two words of fodder rather than acting as a link.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: this Scottish terrier breed is the sort of dog its breeders and trainers are devoted to.

entries.clue: Sucker I see with low debt in need of doing (6,5)

indicators.note: something in need of doing needs working over, so the letters are worked into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone sizing up a gullible borrower with small debts, ripe to be conned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a dupe, which the 'doing' (conning) supports; it is really a sweet you suck. 'With' joins the two parts of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful definition by function: a hard candy is made to be sucked slowly, so it is a sucker.

entries.clue: Working with sailor, one heading to oxbow lake (7)

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its top, so the first letter of oxbow

annotation.surface: A sailor at work heading for an oxbow lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oxbow lake' reads as a single phrase, but oxbow only supplies its first letter and 'lake' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the five Great Lakes of North America, on the Canada–US border.

entries.clue: Ring Republican leader to get Dole out for trial (6)

indicators.note: the leader goes in front, so the first letter of Republican

blocks.note: to dole out cards is to hand them round

annotation.surface: A plea to phone the Republican leader so Bob Dole can be put on trial.
annotation.walkthrough: Bob Dole really was the Republican leader in the US Senate, which makes 'Dole' look like a name; here 'dole out' is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with history: in medieval law, trial by ordeal tested guilt through fire or water.

entries.clue: Linesmen who lament get less upset, I admitted (8)

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order
admitted means let in, so I is let in among the jumbled letters

annotation.surface: Football linesmen grumbling that they are paid less.
annotation.walkthrough: Linesmen here are writers of lines of verse, not assistant referees.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: an elegy is a mournful poem, so its writers produce lines of lament.

entries.clue: Crooked master was first to give class detention (9)

indicators.note: detention means being kept in, so the class is kept inside the other word

blocks.note: a form is a school class

annotation.surface: A corrupt schoolmaster eagerly keeping a class in detention.
annotation.walkthrough: The school picture (master, class, detention) hides a master's degree, and 'was first' goes round the class like pupils kept in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something badly shaped or bent out of true is crooked.

entries.clue: Window bound to make you vertiginous (5-6)

blocks.note: a light is a window pane or opening

annotation.surface: A warning that looking out of a high window will make you dizzy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound' suggests tied up or jumping; here it is the travelling sense, as in homeward bound.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: dizzy, with the giddy sensation of vertigo.

entries.clue: Rake in pine shed close to conservatory (4)

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, as a tree sheds leaves, so a letter is cast off
the close of a word is its end, so the last letter is taken

annotation.surface: A garden rake lying in a pine shed next to the conservatory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pine shed' reads as a wooden shed; pine is the verb and shed the deletion.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to rake in money is to take it in as pay or profit.

entries.clue: Cozy and secure in arms of a revolutionary type (4)

indicators.note: a revolution is a full turn, so the arms are turned round

annotation.surface: A child held close in the arms of a revolutionary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arms' is weapons, not limbs, and the revolutionary is an instruction to turn them round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym covering both halves: warm and comfortable, and also fitting tightly and securely.

entries.clue: Crushing economic crisis making Democrat run (10)

indicators.note: making here means turning into, so the crisis word is changed
run is R in cricket scoring, and it takes the Democrat's place

blocks.note: a depression is an economic slump
r = run in cricket scoring, put in D's place

annotation.surface: A political story: a slump prompting a Democrat to stand for office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like standing for election; it is R, which ousts the D of DEPRESSION.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in noun use: the crushing of a revolt or of feelings is their forcible suppression.

entries.clue: Seed of hope, allegedly (3)

indicators.note: allegedly means according to what is said, so the letter is taken as spoken

blocks.note: the letter P taken from hope and spoken as a word

annotation.surface: A seed of hope, supposedly, in a gloomy time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seed of hope' reads as a stock phrase; the seed is the definition, and the P from hope, said aloud, gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain example: the small round green seed eaten as a vegetable.

entries.clue: Tory tax can’t put off conservative nominee (10)

indicators.note: to put someone off a bus is to get rid of them, so the C is got rid of

blocks.note: to tax = to strain or try

annotation.surface: A Tory candidate complaining that a tax can't be postponed.
annotation.walkthrough: Tory is the British Conservative party, abbreviated Con. 'Put off' looks like postpone; it removes the C.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: someone nominated for an award or seat is one of those competing for it.

entries.clue: Work from musical drama extremely tiresome (7)

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters

blocks.note: a staged drama set to music

annotation.surface: A critic calling a work from a musical drama deadly dull.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a noun (a piece of music); it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: a machine that works is functioning, running as it should.

entries.clue: Club bringing off one up front finds advantage (4)

indicators.note: bringing a player off substitutes them, so one letter leaves the word
up front means at the front, so the first letter is the one removed

blocks.note: a wedge is a golf club
the first letter of WEDGE, removed

annotation.surface: A football club gaining an edge by substituting a striker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One up front' sounds like a lone striker; it is the letter at the front of WEDGE.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: having this over a rival means being slightly ahead of them.

entries.clue: Closely related, but different types of European (7)

blocks.note: a German is one type of European

annotation.surface: A remark that Europeans are kin yet varied.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Different types of European' asks for two versions of the word: a German, and the abbreviation E.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: relevant, pertinent, closely connected to the matter in hand.

entries.clue: Charge to cross Thailand’s frontier’s fair (4)

indicators.note: to cross a border is to go over it, so the charge goes over (around) the T
a frontier is a front edge, so the first letter of Thailand

annotation.surface: A border-crossing toll for Thailand being judged fair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like just, but it is the event.
annotation.definitionFit: A British sense: a summer fundraising event with stalls and games on a village green or school field.

entries.clue: One who’ll have brush with poor ear doctor (9)

indicators.note: poor means in bad condition, so the letters are in a battered order

annotation.surface: A patient having a brush with an incompetent ear specialist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Have a brush with' suggests an encounter; the answer literally holds a paintbrush.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful definition by function: the house painter is the person who wields a brush.

entries.clue: Suits and trunks (5)

blocks.note: lawsuits, matters brought before a court

annotation.surface: A packing list: suits and swimming trunks.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words read as clothing, but suits are lawsuits and trunks are luggage.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: lawsuits heard in court, and boxes or luggage for carrying things.

entries.clue: Fish and game (8)

blocks.note: a party game, reverse hide-and-seek in which seekers pack into the hider's spot

annotation.surface: A menu offering fish and game.
annotation.walkthrough: Fish and game suggests a menu; game is a party game named after how tightly the fish are packed in tins.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: small oily fish packed tightly in tins, and a party game named after them where players cram into one hiding place.

entries.clue: Dressed and ready to roll? (2,4)

blocks.note: wearing one's kit, gear being clothes
of a vehicle, with the transmission engaged

annotation.surface: Someone kitted out and eager to set off.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'ready to roll' is meant literally, of a vehicle ready to move.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: wearing your kit (gear = clothing), and with the transmission engaged so the vehicle can move.

entries.clue: Trap in which a mother might find ruin? (3)

definitions.text: in which a mother might find ruin

blocks.clueFragment: in which a mother might find ruin
blocks.note: points to a spirit's old British nickname, mother's ruin

annotation.surface: A warning about a trap that could ruin a mother.
annotation.walkthrough: Mother's ruin is an old British nickname for the spirit, from its cheap and ruinous popularity in the 18th century.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a snare for catching animals, and the spirit nicknamed mother's ruin.

entries.clue: Bicycle caught in traffic? (6)

indicators.note: to catch words is to hear them, as in 'I didn't catch that'

blocks.note: to bicycle is to pedal; caught = heard, so the same sound spelt another way

annotation.surface: A cyclist stuck in a traffic jam.
annotation.walkthrough: Traffic is the verb, to deal illicitly, and 'caught' means heard rather than trapped.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to sell illicit goods, especially drugs.

entries.clue: One runs Pinter plays in small rep at front (8)

indicators.note: plays means moves freely, as light plays on water, so the letters shift about
in places the jumble inside S and R
at front means at the start, so the first letter of rep

annotation.surface: A small repertory theatre putting on Harold Pinter's plays.
annotation.walkthrough: Harold Pinter the playwright and 'rep' (repertory theatre) set a stage scene; 'One runs' is a noun phrase, one who runs.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the athlete who races over short distances is one who runs.
